div.div: بِلِيلَجٌ , with kesr to the ب and to the first ل, and with fet-h to the second ل; (Msb;) or بَلِيلَجٌ; (so written in some copies of the K, in other copies of which it is omitted;) [Myrobalana Bellerica: (Golius and Freytag:) Terminaria Chebula: Sprengel. hist. rei herb. p. 262: (Freytag:)] a certain well-known Indian medicine; (Msb;) very beneficial to the stomach and to the intestinum rectum. (K.) [For other properties &c. assigned to it, see Ibn-Seenà (Avicenna), book ii. p. 144. See also اِهْلِيلَجٌ, in art. هلج.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
